youtube.title: The CIA Secretly Tried to Steal a Soviet Submarine From 3 Miles Down | Project Azorian
youtube.description:
In March 1968, the Soviet missile submarine K-129 sank with all hands about 1,500 miles northwest of Hawaii, roughly 16,500 feet down. The CIA located it and had a ship built to raise it: the Hughes Glomar Explorer, publicly presented as Howard Hughes's deep-sea mining venture for manganese nodules. In August 1974, the ship's capture vehicle lifted the submarine, but part of it failed and most of the hull fell back to the seabed. Only a forward section was recovered, with the bodies of six Soviet submariners, who were given a filmed burial at sea. When the story leaked in 1975, the CIA would 'neither confirm nor deny' it — the origin of the 'Glomar response.' The CIA's own history of the project was declassified, heavily redacted, in 2010.

📂 Case File #026: Project Azorian

Sources: CIA, "Project AZORIAN: The Story of the Hughes Glomar Explorer" (Studies in Intelligence, 1985; released 2010) via the National Security Archive, Electronic Briefing Book No. 305; Wikipedia, "Glomar Explorer" and its citations.
